notebook: Turn 1. Empty design, 0/50 solves. Feed 3300 mol/s, 16 components, C3-C9. Objective divisor 439 M/yr (=pure n-pentane). Plan: learn column cost scaling and how purities respond, then build a cut tree. Ideas: C6 paraffin blend (970 mol/s) is worth 1181M vs 1349M pure -> blend cheap. C5 mix 618M vs 719 pure. Test one column first to see simulator output format.

notebook:
Turn 2. Feed 3300 mol/s, 16 comps C3-C9. Objective = (revenue - column cost)/439 $M/yr.

Component values if pure ($M/yr): C3mix blend 91, C4mix 186 (pure sum 207), n-butane 166, C5mix 618 (pure 717), 22DMB 284, 2MP 389, 3MP 343, nC6 332, MCP 144, cyclohex 322, C6paraffin blend 1181 (pure 1349), C6naphthene blend 396 (pure 466), nC7 332, nC8 358, nC9 103. Total pure ~3611.

Lesson turn1: 40-stage column at R=3.0 cost $194.6M/yr - huge! Column cost dominates; must use few columns with modest reflux, or cost eats revenue. Two outlets at that split were impure (worth 0).

Plan: explore cost vs reflux/stages. Cheap columns may be better than many pure cuts. Considering blend strategy: C6 paraffin mix (1181) + C6 naphthene mix (396) + C5 mix + C4 mix + C3 mix. Turn2: build 3-column tree to see costs of multiple columns.

note: Kill the two sub-columns and shrink the main cut to a cheap 30-stage/-/1.5 column to measure the minimum cost floor and see how one cheap column splits. This establishes a cost baseline before committing to a separation train.
notebook:

Component pure values ($M/yr): C3mix blend 73, C4mix 186, nC4 166, C5mix 618, 22DMB 284, 2MP 389, 3MP 343, nC6 332, MCP 144, cyclohex 322, C6par mix 1181, C6 naph mix 396, nC7 332, nC8 358, nC9 103. Total pure ~3611.

KEY LESSON t1-2: cost is huge. 40 stages R=3.0 -> $194.6M/yr; 30 stages R=2.0 -> $34-97M/yr depending on size. Cost scales strongly with stages and reflux. With 3 columns we were at -$325M/yr revenue 0. So must get pure/blend streams, not just cuts.

NBP order: C2=184.6, C3==225.4, C3=231.0, iC4=261.3, nC4=272.7, iC5=301.0, nC5=309.2, 22DMB=322.9, 2MP=333.4, 3MP=336.4, nC6=341.9, MCP=345.0, chx=353.9, nC7=371.6, nC8=398.8, nC9=424.0.

Blend targets: C3mix(propyl+propane), C4mix(iC4+nC4), C5mix(iC5+nC5), C6par mix(22DMB+2MP+3MP+nC6), C6naph mix(MCP+chx), then nC7,nC8,nC9 pure. Note nC6/MCP close (3.1K) - hard split; may be easier to lump but blends don't allow that.

This turn: measure cost floor of one cheap 30-stage R=1.5 column.

Cost is enormous: 30-stage R=1.5 col = $121.5M/yr; 40-stage R=3 = $194.6M/yr. So must use FEW columns and make blend cuts.

PRODUCT PLAN (9 products, 8 columns): C2(4), C3mix(63), C4mix(176), C5mix(611), C6par mix(1147), C6naph mix(397), nC7(332), nC8(359), nC9(104) = ~$3193M/yr revenue. If cost ~$800M net ~$2400 => reward ~5.5.

Diff=95% (blend) or 99% (premium 1.2x). Hard splits: C3=/C3 (5.6K), nC6/MCP (3.1K), MCP/chx (8.9K), 2MP/3MP (3K but same blend).

Feed value math (factor = 28.8 $M per mol/s per $/mol): total pure value if all 16 separated = ~$3615M (divisor 439).
Groups: C2 34 ($4M nuisance), C3 mix 286 (~$73M), C4 mix 544 (~$186M), C5 mix 695 (~$619M), C6 paraffin mix 970 (~$550M), C6 naphthene mix 269 (~$180M), n-C7 205 (~$92M), n-C8 233 (~$100M), n-C9 62 (~$29M).
So the big money is C5 (~$619M) and C6 (~$730M combined). Even 4-5 columns can capture ~$1500M if cuts are sharp enough to hit 95%.

Plan: rebuild a MINIMAL, cheap, correctly-configured train: (1) root cuts light C2/C3/C4 overhead vs C5+ bottoms cheaply; measure. Keep stages/reflux low, dp 0.1. Use blends where they qualify to avoid extra columns. Avoid overspending solves; each config change costs 1 solve per distinct column.
